title: Arrays and Pointers
description: Array decay, pointer indexing/traversal, multidimensional arrays as pointers, and passing arrays to functions.
objectives: Traverse an array using pointer arithmetic instead of indexing
Understand how multidimensional arrays relate to pointers
Pass arrays (including multidimensional ones) to functions correctly

content.heading: Array Decay and Pointer Traversal
content.body:
'Array decay' refers to the rule that, in most expressions (though notably not sizeof(arr) or &arr), an array name is automatically converted to a pointer to its first element. This means int arr[5] and int *p = arr; behave almost identically for indexing purposes, but they are not the same type: sizeof(arr) gives the whole array's size in bytes, while sizeof(p) gives just a pointer's size, regardless of how many elements p happens to point at — this distinction is exactly what causes the classic 'wrong array size inside a function' bug, since a function parameter declared as int arr[] is actually treated as int *arr, having already lost the original size information.

Traversing an array via pointer arithmetic (for (int *p = arr; p < arr + n; p++) { use *p; }) is equivalent to index-based traversal (for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) { use arr[i]; }) and was historically sometimes preferred for performance on older compilers, though modern compilers generally optimize both forms identically.

content.heading: Multidimensional Arrays and Passing to Functions
content.body:
A 2D array int grid[3][4] decays (when passed to a function) into a pointer to an array of 4 ints (int (*)[4]), not a plain int**, an important and frequently confusing distinction — the function parameter must specify at least the inner dimension size, void process(int grid[][4], int rows), so the compiler knows how far apart each row is in memory.

When passing any array to a function, always pass its length (or, for 2D arrays, both dimensions) as a separate parameter, since the array parameter itself carries no size information after decaying to a pointer.

content.explanation: sumRow demonstrates pointer-arithmetic-based traversal as an alternative to arr[i]. printGrid's parameter must specify the inner dimension (3) so the compiler can correctly compute each row's memory offset.

keyPoints: An array name decays to a pointer to its first element in most expressions, but not in sizeof(arr) or &arr
arr[i] indexing and pointer-arithmetic traversal (*(p+i)) are equivalent
A 2D array parameter must specify its inner dimension so the compiler knows the row stride
Always pass array length(s) as separate parameters — the decayed pointer carries no size information
commonMistakes: Using sizeof(arr) inside a function that received arr as a parameter, expecting the original array's full size
Omitting the inner dimension when declaring a 2D array function parameter
Confusing a decayed 2D array pointer (int (*)[N]) with a plain int**, which is a genuinely different type
